description: A `struct` type name colliding with a user procedure raises `ol-duplicate-definition` at phase-1 registration: `foo` is already declared on line 1, so `struct foo` cannot also register a constructor of that name. Ruling #833 rule 6 gives a name the LEARNER already declared its own code, distinct from `ol-reserved-word`'s "OpenLogo owns this name". What this fixture pins is the observable behaviour: the two declarations differ in KIND (`define` then `struct`), which is the cross-kind half of `spec/error-model.md:126` ("a procedure and a struct with the same name in either order"), and `params.original_span` points at the `define`. It does NOT prove the runtime keeps a single first-declaration map internally — two maps with an explicit cross-kind lookup would produce the identical diagnostic, and no source-level fixture can tell them apart. `struct-then-define-duplicate` pins the opposite order, and `data/check/duplicate-definition-across-declaration-slots` pins the same program at check stage. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
